appraisal_events.evidence: Swann coupa l'effet de Brichot à la grande fureur de la maîtresse de la maison, en répondant qu'on voulût bien l'excuser de s'intéresser si peu à Blanche de Castille, mais qu'il avait quelque chose à demander au peintre.
appraisal_events.explanation: Swann cuts off Brichot's anecdote before its intended punchline, denying him his rhetorical moment and redirecting the table to his own question, which provokes the hostess's anger.

appraisal_events.evidence: Toute la table éclata de rire. — Quand je vous disais qu'on ne peut pas garder son sérieux avec lui, dit Mme Verdurin à Forcheville. Au moment où on s'y attend le moins, il vous sort une calembredaine.
appraisal_events.explanation: Cottard's pun draws laughter from the whole table, and Mme Verdurin explicitly praises his wit to Forcheville, elevating his standing as the salon's entertaining wit.

status_effects.explanation: Brichot's story is cut short before its climax, and his elaborate approach to Swann yields no payoff, leaving him locally deflated at the table.
By cutting off Brichot and provoking the hostess's open fury, Swann incurs a local social cost within the codified etiquette of the Verdurin salon.
Cottard is clearly elevated: his quip produces collective laughter and explicit verbal praise from the hostess.

ambiguities: Swann's interruption of Brichot can be read either as assertive control of the conversation or as a breach of salon propriety; the status effect follows the explicitly narrated consequence (the hostess's fury) rather than assuming Swann intended offense.
